title: Cooperative catalysis (rate ~ e^2) makes a catalysis-induced condensate on a consumed fuel hollow into a growing enzyme ring with a refuelled interior; the same droplet on a fuel reservoir stays solid
summary: world.py is c23's CIPS-fuel world with catalysis made second order in the enzyme (cat = kc F e^2 (1-p), kc=2), De=0.1, chi=3, conserved enzyme (d=0). The dilute state is then stable, so a planted enzyme disk (R=10, mechanism test only) survives in a uniform background. On the consumed fuel (kF=0.2) it hollows by t~750 into a ring: enzyme ~0.95 in the ring and ~0.05 inside, fuel ~0.03 in the ring and re-grown to ~0.62 inside vs 0.97 outside (ring_fields.png, cut at t=2000); the ring keeps widening as it takes up dilute enzyme (area 305 -> 2846 px by t=4875 at 256^2) and never breaks within 5000 t. With fuel held at 1 the same droplet stays a solid disk and satellite droplets nucleate around it, so the hole is made by the body's own fuel consumption. At a finer effective grid (Lsc=5, dt 0.05; ring_growth_res5_noise.png, middle row) the ring persists and is rounder (the diamond is grid anisotropy). From noise (e0=0.15, 192^2) 32 solid droplets form and stay below the size at which they hollow (count flat t=800-3900), so no rings and no splits from noise yet.
